theme: Hezekiah’s great reform, Temple worship restored
readingInstruction: Read 2 Chronicles 29:1-32:33. Hezekiah reopens the temple, restores the Passover, and trusts God when Sennacherib invades. Read for the extraordinary Passover, where the whole kingdom seeks the LORD, and note 30:18-20.
settingTheScene: Hezekiah is the Chronicler’s greatest reformer. He begins in the first month of his first year, opening the doors of the temple. Unlike the account in Kings, which emphasizes Sennacherib’s invasion, the Chronicler spends three chapters on the temple’s cleansing and the great Passover. You read the Sennacherib story in Isaiah in Unit 12. Here it is brief, and in this book it is the reward of faithfulness.
observation: “In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them” (29:3).
“For our fathers have been unfaithful and have done what was evil in the sight of the LORD our God” (29:6).
“Be not like your fathers and your brothers, who were faithless to the LORD” (30:7).
“But some men of Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem” (30:11).
“May the good LORD pardon everyone who sets his heart to seek God, the LORD, the God of his fathers, even though not according to the sanctuary’s rules of cleanness” (30:18-19).
“And the LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people” (30:20).
“So there was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the time of Solomon… there had been nothing like this” (30:26).
“Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or dismayed… for there is one greater with us than with him” (32:7).
interpretation:
Hezekiah acts at once. In the first month of his first year, he reopens the temple, and the priests spend sixteen days cleansing it. His words to the Levites: “Do not now be negligent, for the LORD has chosen you to stand in his presence.” Then the temple is rededicated with burnt offerings and with singing, “the song to the LORD began also, and the trumpets.” The people bring thank offerings, so many that the priests need help.

Then he does something unusual: he invites the northern tribes, now in ruin under Assyria, to come to Jerusalem to keep the Passover. Couriers go throughout Israel, from Beersheba to Dan. Some laugh at them. But others humble themselves and come. The result is a massive celebration, for two weeks, with joy that Jerusalem had not seen since Solomon.

One detail is gracious. Many who came had not purified themselves according to the rules. Hezekiah prays: “May the good LORD pardon everyone who sets his heart to seek God, even though not according to the sanctuary’s rules of cleanness.” And the LORD heard and healed the people. God cares about the heart above ritual precision, though he does not dismiss ritual.

When Sennacherib invades, the Chronicler tells it in a few verses. Hezekiah strengthens the walls, digs a tunnel to bring water into the city, and encourages the people: “With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God, to help us and to fight our battles.” He and Isaiah cry to heaven, and an angel destroys the Assyrian army. The chapter ends with a hint of pride in Hezekiah’s heart, which he repents of, and then notes his prosperity. “God left him to himself, in order to test him and to know all that was in his heart.” Even the best king is human.
connection: Hebrews 4:16: “Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace.” 1 Corinthians 5:7-8: Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed. Luke 15:20 shows the father welcoming the returning son. Joel 2:12-13 calls for returning with all your heart. 1 John 4:4: “He who is in you is greater than he who is in the world.” Romans 10:1-3 speaks of zeal for God, rightly understood.
application:
Do the first thing first: what is one area where God’s “house” in your life needs to be cleaned out and opened?

Invite someone who is far from God to come with you to worship.

When you fear, remember: “There is one greater with us than with him.”
prayerPrompts: Ask God to pardon everyone who sets their heart to seek him, including you.
Ask him to help you cleanse what is unclean in your life.
